name: 11 Nimmt: Two Hot Piles
summary: Each turn, place one card from a hidden hand on one of two shared piles where it fits; a player with no legal placement must take a pile's ox-heads as penalty, though taking a pile of 3 or more cards earns a bull worth -2. The lowest penalty minus twice bulls wins.

player.meaning: The cards (numbers) in this player's private hand
Bulls earned by taking piles of 3 or more cards; each is worth -2 at the end
Final score so far: penalty - 2 * bulls (lower is better)

game.meaning: H, which is also the number of rounds: 9 with 3 players, 8 with 4 players
The shuffled undealt cards, used only during setup
Cards set aside unseen that take no part in the game
The cards in Pile A, in play order; the last card is the top
The cards in Pile B, in play order; the last card is the top
Number of cards in Pile A
Number of cards in Pile B
Cards from taken piles, now out of the game
The seat whose turn it is
Scratch counter of turns taken this round
Description of the latest turn: who played, which card, which pile, and whether it was a take

setup: Set deck_size N = 30 and hand_size H = 9 with 3 players, or N = 40 and H = 8 with 4 players.
Fill deck with the cards 1 to N.
Each card's ox value is 3 if it is 11, 22 or 33; otherwise 2 if it is a multiple of 5; otherwise 1.
Deal each player H cards into hand, each one drawn at random from deck and removed from it.
Draw one random card from deck into pile_a (top_a = that card, size_a = 1, ox_a = its ox), and one into pile_b (top_b, size_b = 1, ox_b = its ox). Both piles are public.
Move every remaining deck card into set_aside (1 card with 3 players, 6 with 4). They are never seen and never used.
Every player starts with penalty 0, bulls 0 and score 0, and round = 1.
Sync each player's hand to that player only.

round.answer: One option naming a card from own hand and a pile, e.g. '17 on A'. If the seat holds at least one placement (card c fits pile X, meaning (c - top_X) mod N is between 1 and 10, and size_X < 5), only placements are offered. Otherwise every card in hand on A and on B is offered, each marked as a take.
round.effect: Records the chosen card c and pile X

Remove c from hand. If c fits X ((c - top_X) mod N in 1..10) and size_X < 5 (a placement): append c to pile_X, top_X = c, size_X += 1, ox_X += ox(c). Otherwise (a take): penalty += ox_X; if size_X >= 3 then bulls += 1; move all of pile_X into discarded; pile_X = [c], top_X = c, size_X = 1, ox_X = ox(c). The other pile is unchanged. Then score = penalty - 2 * bulls, and last_play describes the move.
Announce last_play, both piles (cards, top, size, ox total) and every player's penalty, bulls and score.
Repeat steps 2 to 5 until turns_in_round = number_of_players.
Each player is sent their own hand and the public state.
If round > hand_size, end the game; otherwise continue.

ending.decided_by: Each player's final score is penalty - 2 * bulls. The lowest final score wins, so ranking is by its negative. Players tied for lowest share the win, which is a draw among them.

rules.text: With 3 players the deck is cards 1 to 30 and each hand is 9 cards; with 4 players the deck is cards 1 to 40 and each hand is 8 cards.
Cards 11, 22 and 33 carry 3 ox-heads, every other multiple of 5 carries 2, and all other cards carry 1 (e.g. 11 -> 3, 25 -> 2, 7 -> 1).
At setup two face-up cards start pile_a and pile_b, each of size 1 with ox equal to its card; the remaining 1 (3 players) or 6 (4 players) cards go to set_aside and are never used.
All players start with penalty 0 and bulls 0.
A card c fits a pile with top t when (c - t) mod N is between 1 and 10 inclusive; with N = 30 and top 25, cards 26 to 30 and 1 to 5 fit, and 6 and 25 do not.
A pile has room when it holds fewer than 5 cards; a pile of 5 cards accepts no placement.
When a player holds at least one placement (a card that fits a pile with room), only placements are offered to them.
When a player places card c on pile X, c leaves the hand, becomes top_X, size_X rises by 1 and ox_X rises by ox(c); the other pile is unchanged.
When a player holds no placement, they must take: they may choose any card from hand and either pile.
When a player takes pile X, their penalty rises by ox_X, the pile's cards go to discarded, and the chosen card becomes the pile's only card (size 1, ox equal to its ox).
When the taken pile had 3 or more cards the taker gains 1 bull; when it had 1 or 2 cards they gain none.
In round r, seats act one after another starting with seat ((r - 1) mod number_of_players) + 1 and wrapping round in seat order.
Every turn removes exactly one card from the acting player's hand, so all hands are empty after round H.
The game ends after exactly H rounds (9 with 3 players, 8 with 4).
A player's final score is penalty - 2 * bulls; e.g. penalty 7 with 2 bulls scores 3.
Cards left in the two piles at the end count against nobody.
The player with the lowest final score wins; players tied for lowest share a draw.

offers.question: Your turn: choose a card and a pile
offers.options: If the seat holds any placement: exactly the pairs 'c on A' where c is in hand, (c - top_a) mod N is in 1..10 and size_a < 5, plus the pairs 'c on B' meeting the same test against top_b and size_b. If the seat holds no placement: every card in hand paired with A and with B, each labelled as a take (e.g. 'take A with 17').

choices.why: The source defines the deck and hand only for 3 and 4 players, and the designer suggests 3. With fewer, there is too little contention over the two piles; the rules define no larger deck.

choices.what: No talk step before each turn
choices.why: The source has no communication phase, and adding one would be adding a mechanic. Play is about hand management: keeping low-risk cards, timing takes while piles are small, and taking a pile of 3 or more cards when the bull's -2 outweighs its ox-heads.

choices.what: Card and pile are chosen as one combined option
choices.why: The rules ask for both together, and a single choice lets the offers enforce the placement-first rule exactly.
The engine ranks the highest value first, and the rules want the lowest penalty - 2 * bulls.

choices.what: A running score attribute updated every turn
choices.why: It makes the standing observable and testable during play.

simplifications.what: The rotating start seat and sequential turns are built as a repeat loop over current_seat with a per-turn update
simplifications.why: Each turn changes the piles before the next seat chooses, so each turn's update must run before the next ask.

simplifications.what: Whether a move is a take is worked out at update time by testing if the chosen card fits the chosen pile with room
simplifications.why: The offers allow non-placements only when no placement exists, so this test is equivalent to the rule.
